zh.label: 片刻随记 · 08
zh.title: AI 时代，互联网人做一人公司 OPC 的大机会，原来藏在这里！
zh.excerpt: 把产品、设计、开发与运营接起来：先解决自己的真实需要，再用 App、网页与 AI，把小产品带向大世界。
zh.content:
![小产品，也可以连接大世界](/assets/notes/2026-09-17-opc-opportunity/cover.png)

“以后跟 AI 说一声就行了，谁还打开你的 App？”

这个问题值得思考。对有产品、设计、开发或运营经验的互联网人来说，AI 时代，做面向全球的小产品，值得重新认真考虑。

借助 AI，把产品、设计、开发和运营这些环节尽可能接起来。

路线也很具体：先满足自己的真实需求，用 iOS 把核心体验做好，用 H5 让世界各地的人容易发现、试用和分享，再用持续价值慢慢建立收入。

不需要第一天就喊着改变世界。先让世界某个角落的一小群人，觉得这东西挺好，明天还想用。

## 01 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜互联网人的老本事，终于能给自己用了

做过互联网的人，多少都练过一些本领：看需求、理流程、改文案、盯体验、想办法让人留下来。

只是过去，这些能力常常分别放在不同岗位里。轮到自己做产品，才发现还缺好几位同事。

AI 让我看到的机会，是一个人能接住更多环节了。原型、代码、翻译、测试思路、内容整理、运营，都可以用 AI。你当然仍要判断和验收，但一个想法从脑子走到可体验的版本，没必要每一步都等人到齐。

对我来说，机会正在这里：以前积累的产品判断、设计，终于有了更短的落地路径。

不过，未来做得出产品的人也会更多（现在会用 AI 做出上线产品的还很少）。光靠“我也做了一个”，很快就不够用了。

真正需要回答的是：怎么让人知道你？怎么让人用一次？怎么让人用过一次，还会回来？

这个问题，我先问自己。

## 02 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜第一个用户，不用找，就是我自己

我给自己定的一个原则是：自己永远是产品的第一个用户，先满足自己的需求。

我做的这些小产品，各自在我的生活里占了一个位置。

一休冥想，是我睡前会打开的那个。每天中午，我会听着它入睡；夜里提前醒来，也会继续听着，慢慢再睡过去。对我来说，打开它的理由很直接：此刻想听一段声音，安静下来。

三慢问道·道德经，是我每天会读一章的那个。我尤其喜欢“对我们的启发”和“生活中的道”。古文和翻译读完了，我还想知道：这句话，跟今天的我有什么关系？那些把道理带回日常的部分，正是我愿意继续读的理由。

不二·认识自己，像一本可以翻翻的“自己的使用说明书”。我把它当作自我观察的入口，借它想一想自己的习惯、感受和选择。它给我一个理解自己的角度，答案仍然要放回生活里看。

虾子曰，是我每天早上会看一眼的那个。起床后，我想知道世界发生了什么；每天不同风格的 9 张精美热点海报（风格提供：虾子曰艺术风格图鉴 App），让我保持对世界的好奇，以及对美的追求。

> 一休：先照顾身体，安顿情绪，再继续前行。
不二：不评判，没有好坏对错，接纳高峰与低谷，拥抱完整而非完美。
三慢：慢下来，慢慢来，慢慢成为。如水，向内扎根，向外流动；顺应变化，不失本心。

这些需求听起来都不宏大，却会一次次出现。我觉得，一个小产品能在人的一天里占住一个真实的位置，已经很有意义。

先让自己离不开，再去找和自己有相似需要的人。

当然，我喜欢用，还不能证明别人愿意付费。接下来仍要请真实用户试，听他们为什么留下、为什么离开。但至少起点是一个活生生的需要。

## 03 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜App 和 H5，可以各干各擅长的事

H5 做一个容易进来的门面（也方便做 GEO、SEO，以及未来潜在的合作），App 做一个值得留下来的房间。

这里说的 H5，就是能通过链接打开的网页体验。

别人看到一张分享卡、一篇文章，点进网页，先知道你在解决什么问题，最好还能体验到一点价值。

而对需要反复使用的场景，我更愿意在 App 里打磨连续体验。

拿一休冥想的方向举例：设想一个用户从微信、从网页试听一段自然声，发现适合自己；之后希望随时回来，方便地开始聆听。网页可以承担第一次相遇，App 可以承接长期使用。

所谓全球化，可以先选一个具体人群、一个场景、一两个语言市场（一开始中英文就行）。页面、示例、应用商店介绍，都围绕他们来做。

能被全球访问，只是起点；被某一群人需要，才是生意的开头。

## 04 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜为什么我会优先做 iOS（iPhone）

资源有限时，先在哪个平台验证收费，值得想清楚。

RevenueCat 的《2026 订阅 App 报告》在其样本中观察到，App Store 在下载到付费的转化、早期每次安装收入等方面有优势；但不同环节的差距并不一样，进入试用后的付费转化，两边更接近。[1]

我的选择会是：对适合订阅、需要反复使用的个人产品，先用 iOS 验证付费意愿，把有限精力集中起来。

如果目标用户主要用安卓，或者主要服务国内用户（微信小程序），或者任务天然适合浏览器，这个顺序当然要变。不过友情提醒一下，安卓手机厂商太多了，需要做认证、开发适配，以及上架和维护不同应用商店、对接收付款等等，工作量指数级上升。

## 05 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜订阅是慢生意，慢在哪里？

我喜欢订阅的地方，是它允许一个小产品，通过不断把事情做好，积累一段长期关系。（依然有很多免费的功能。）

用户第一次付费，可能是好奇，也可能是期待。下个月还愿意付，问题就直接多了：“这段时间，你到底帮到我了吗？”

所以，我愿意把“只要 App 有价值，就能跑通”说得更具体一点：它要持续解决问题，有人愿意持续付费，留下来的收入也要足以支持你继续做。

这才有机会形成商业闭环。

订阅也不适合硬套。只需要解决一次的事情，可以考虑买断或按次收费；有持续使用理由的产品，再认真设计续费。

## 06 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜Siri 越能干，App 就越没价值吗？

这是我最想聊的地方。

苹果在 2026 年 6 月公布的 Siri AI 方向中，明确提到更强的跨 App 查找和执行能力。[2] 开发者可以通过 App Intents 等机制，把 App 的动作和内容交给系统识别、调用。[3]

这里需要分清：这是有接入条件的能力，不等于 Siri 已经无条件打通所有 App。苹果发布时也列出了测试安排及设备、语言、地区限制，具体使用仍要看实际开放情况。

但这个方向给了我一个新的观察角度：用户少点几次图标，并不等于背后完成任务的产品失去了价值。

假设未来用户说：“帮我开始一段三分钟的放松练习。”

这句话由谁听懂是一件事。练习内容从哪里来、声音是否合适、播放是否稳定、个人记忆怎样保存，是另一组事情。这个场景只是设想，并不表示一休已经接入或支持这条 Siri 指令。

我更愿意把 AI 助手想成一个越来越聪明的前台。

前台能听懂客人要什么，能少让客人绕路。可到了房间，热水有没有、床舒不舒服，还是要有人把它做好。

![网页、App、AI：通向同一种服务的不同入口 · 概念示意](/assets/notes/2026-09-17-opc-opportunity/entryways.png)

当然，前台也可能自己提供一些服务。简单、通用、没有积累的功能，确实可能被系统直接覆盖。

所以我的判断有一个前提：更值得做的，是有独特内容、可靠能力或持续体验的 App，并且让这些能力更容易被调用。

## 07 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜小产品，连接有趣的灵魂

AI 时代让我兴奋的，不是一天能生成多少个 App。

是那些过去卡在“我一个人做不了”的想法，现在有机会走到真实用户面前。

一个自己每天都遇到的小问题。一个自己愿意反复打开的 iOS 产品。一个能让人理解和体验的网页入口。一群愿意回来的人。一笔能支持继续改进的收入。

每一步都要验证。可这些步骤，已经构成了一条我愿意认真走的路。

我不指望一上线，全世界就来排队。

我更期待的是，有一天，一个不认识的人，用另一种语言告诉我：“这个东西，我每天都在用。”

那时，我自己的一个小需要，就和世界上另一个人的生活连在了一起。

想抓住的一人公司机会，可以从这里开始。

en.label: FIELD NOTES · 08
en.title: The Big Opportunity for Internet Professionals Building One-Person Companies in the AI Era
en.excerpt: Connect product, design, development, and operations: begin with a real need of your own, then use apps, the web, and AI to bring a small product to a wider world.
en.content:
![Small apps can connect to a big world](/assets/notes/2026-09-17-opc-opportunity/cover.png)

“If people can simply tell AI what they want, who will still open your app?”

That question is worth thinking about. For people with experience in product, design, development, or operations, the AI era makes small products for a global audience worth taking seriously again.

AI can help one person connect product, design, development, and operations. The route can be concrete: start with a real need of your own, build the core experience well on iOS, use the web to make it easy for people around the world to discover, try, and share it, then build revenue slowly through continuing value.

You do not need to announce on day one that you will change the world. First, help a small group somewhere in the world think, “This is good. I want to use it again tomorrow.”

## 01 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜The Skills Internet Professionals Already Have Can Finally Serve Their Own Products

People who have worked on internet products have usually learned a set of useful skills: recognizing needs, organizing flows, refining copy, watching the experience, and finding ways to help people stay.

In the past, those abilities were often spread across different roles. When you build your own product, you suddenly realize you are still missing several colleagues.

The opportunity I see in AI is that one person can now carry more of the chain. Prototypes, code, translation, test plans, content organization, and operations can all be supported by AI. Judgment and acceptance still belong to you, but an idea no longer has to wait for a full team at every step before it becomes something people can experience.

For me, this is the opportunity: the product judgment and design experience accumulated over the years now have a shorter path to reality.

More people will also become able to build products. Merely saying “I made one too” will soon be insufficient.

The real questions are: how will people find you, try the product once, and want to return after that first use?

I begin by asking myself.

## 02 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜You Do Not Have to Search for the First User: It Is You

I follow one principle: I am always the first user of my product. I start by meeting a need of my own.

Each of my small products occupies a place in my life.

Yixiu Meditation is what I open before sleep. I listen to it during a midday nap; when I wake too early at night, I keep listening and gradually fall asleep again. My reason for opening it is direct: I want to hear a sound and settle down now.

Wendao is what I read one chapter from each day. I especially value the sections that ask what the text can teach us and how its ideas return to daily life.

Bu'er Human Design is like a personal manual I can browse. I use it as an entry point for observing my habits, feelings, and choices. It offers one perspective; the answers still have to be tested in life.

Xiazi is what I look at each morning. Its nine carefully made news posters in changing visual styles help me stay curious about the world and committed to beauty.

> Yixiu: care for the body, settle the emotions, then continue forward.
Bu'er: do not judge; accept peaks and valleys, and embrace wholeness rather than perfection.
Wendao: slow down, take your time, slowly become. Like water, root inward and flow outward; adapt without losing yourself.

These needs are not grand, but they return again and again. A small product that earns a real place in someone's day is already meaningful.

First, make something you would miss. Then find people with a similar need.

My own use does not prove that others will pay. Real users still need to try it, and I need to listen to why they stay or leave. But the starting point is at least a living need.

## 03 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜Apps and the Web Can Each Do What They Do Best

The web can be an easy front door, while the app becomes a room worth staying in. A linked web experience also supports discovery through search and future partnerships.

People may encounter a shared card or an article, open a page, understand what problem you solve, and ideally experience a little value immediately.

For situations that invite repeated use, I prefer to refine the continuous experience inside the app.

Consider Yixiu: someone hears a nature sound through WeChat or the web and finds that it suits them. Later, they want to return at any time and start listening easily. The web can handle the first meeting; the app can support the longer relationship.

Going global can begin with one specific audience, one scenario, and one or two language markets. Chinese and English are enough at first. The pages, examples, and app-store listing can all speak to those people.

Being accessible worldwide is only the starting point. Being needed by a particular group is where a business begins.

## 04 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜Why I Would Start with iOS (iPhone)

When resources are limited, it is worth deciding carefully where to test willingness to pay.

RevenueCat's State of Subscription Apps 2026 observed advantages for the App Store in measures such as download-to-paid conversion and early revenue per install, while some later-stage differences were smaller.[1]

My choice is to use iOS first to test willingness to pay for personal products that suit subscriptions and repeated use, concentrating limited energy.

If the intended users mainly use Android, if the product primarily serves people in China through a WeChat mini program, or if the task naturally belongs in the browser, the order should change. Android also brings substantial work across device certification, adaptation, multiple stores, payments, and ongoing maintenance.

## 05 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜Subscriptions Are a Slow Business. What Makes Them Slow?

What I like about subscriptions is that a small product can accumulate a long relationship by continuing to do its job well, while still keeping many functions free.

A first payment may come from curiosity or expectation. If someone pays again next month, the question becomes direct: “Did you actually help me during this time?”

So “a valuable app can work as a business” needs a more precise definition: it must keep solving a problem, people must keep choosing to pay, and the remaining income must be enough to support continued work.

Only then does a sustainable loop become possible.

Subscriptions should not be forced onto every product. A one-time problem may suit a purchase or per-use fee; products with an ongoing reason to return deserve thoughtful renewal design.

## 06 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜If Siri Becomes More Capable, Do Apps Become Less Valuable?

This is the part I most want to discuss.

In June 2026, Apple described a direction for Siri AI with stronger cross-app finding and action capabilities.[2] Through mechanisms such as App Intents, developers can make an app's actions and content recognizable and callable by the system.[3]

This distinction matters: these abilities have integration requirements. They do not mean Siri can already access every app without conditions. Apple's announcement also described testing plans and device, language, and region limits; actual use depends on availability.

Still, the direction suggests another way to look at value: fewer taps on an app icon do not mean the product completing the task has lost its value.

Imagine a user saying, “Start a three-minute relaxation practice.” Understanding the sentence is one job. Providing the practice, selecting appropriate audio, playing it reliably, and preserving personal history are another set of jobs. This is a hypothetical scenario; it does not mean Yixiu already supports that Siri command.

I think of the AI assistant as an increasingly intelligent front desk. It can understand what a guest wants and shorten the route. But once the guest reaches the room, someone still has to make sure the hot water works and the bed is comfortable.

![Web, apps, and AI are different entrances to the same service — concept illustration](/assets/notes/2026-09-17-opc-opportunity/entryways.png)

The front desk may also provide some services itself. Simple, generic functions with no accumulated value may indeed be absorbed by the system.

That is why my judgment has a condition: the apps most worth building offer distinctive content, reliable capability, or a continuing experience—and make those capabilities easier to call.

## 07 / SMALL APPS, BIG WORLD｜Small Products Connect Interesting Souls

What excites me about the AI era is not how many apps can be generated in a day.

It is that ideas once blocked by “I cannot build this alone” can now reach real users.

A small problem I encounter every day. An iOS product I willingly reopen. A web entrance that helps people understand and experience it. A group of people who return. Revenue that supports continued improvement.

Every step needs validation. Together, though, these steps form a path I want to follow seriously.

I do not expect the whole world to line up as soon as I launch.

What I hope for is that one day, someone I have never met tells me in another language: “I use this every day.”

Then one small need of mine will have connected with another person's life somewhere in the world.

The one-person-company opportunity I want to pursue can begin here.
